{"basis":"measured","confidence":0.95,"fact_type":"finding","name":"ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): the server expires an MCP session after 300 s idle, taking its seat lease with it; the proxy reads "Session not found" as "server died", re-handshakes to the SAME server, and gets a NEW seat, so every claim made under the old seat reads `gone` while its client is still working","source":"dev_reflow2 hub session, root-cause skill; controlled probe against reflow2's shared server (pid 1448716, release 0.66.0), 2026-09-23 10:13–10:20 UTC","statement":"RUN AS THE SKILL, 2026-09-23, on Anthony's instruction ("Do proper root cause").
① OBSERVED (fact:two-active-sessions-claims-both-read-gone-2026-09-22): two actively working sessions' claims both read `gone`.
② PRECEDENT: fact:defect-claim-liveness-is-the-servers-pid-not-the-sessions and fact:defect-a-tool-minted-seat-is-never-registered-so-gone-is-still-unreachable (both 2026-08-07/08), and chg:seat-liveness-is-the-session-20260808. Those fixed the OPPOSITE direction, gone clients reading live, by leasing a seat per SESSION and reading `gone` once the lease is released. That fix is correct for what it models; what it models is the transport session, not the client.
③ CANDIDATES: (A) the sessionless transport builds a handler, and so a seat, per REQUEST; (B) the transport session is shorter-lived than the client and is replaced underneath it; (C) claims made without an explicit seat pick up one the server later drops; (D) the observation is stale.
④⑤ MEASURED. A was REFUTED: two consecutive calls on one live connection returned the same seat (…:6d10d5c0). B was CONFIRMED by a controlled probe: seat A …:403d875b took a claim (read `live`), idled 330 s, then called again. The seat was now …:71d4ba4f, the claim read `gone`, and the proxy logged, verbatim: "the shared reflow2 server stopped answering (the shared reflow2 server answered 404 Not Found: Not Found: Session not found); starting a replacement and retrying once", followed by "attaching to the shared reflow2 server … pid=1448716", the SAME server. The code path: rmcp LocalSessionManager DEFAULT_KEEP_ALIVE = 300 s → idle session worker quits → handler dropped → SeatLease released → registry_verdict returns Gone. proxy.rs Upstream::send treats the 404 as a dead server and re-initializes. C is a consequence of B, not separate. D was refuted by the live measurement.
SIDE MEASUREMENT: the first call after the idle took ~80 s (t=351 s expected, t=434 s observed), spent in the needless replace-the-server detour. A client idle for five minutes pays over a minute on its next tool call.
⑥ CLASS: an identity meant to last as long as the CLIENT is bound to a TRANSPORT session whose lifetime the transport chooses (5 min idle), and the proxy silently swaps the transport session underneath. It also resets the other per-session state (read-hint memory, session read/write counters). The instance is claims; the class is "session-scoped state lives on the wrong object". It would have stopped the 2026-09-22 report and any claim held by an agent that waits more than five minutes, which covers builds, CI and a person thinking.
⑦ NOT YET PINNED BY A TEST: the probe above is the reproduction to turn into one (idle past keep-alive, assert same seat and `live`). It fails on today's build, as measured.
⑧ THE FIX AT THE CAUSE (not built, stated for the owner): make the seat belong to the CLIENT, not the HTTP session. The `--shared` proxy is a long-lived process per client, so it mints or holds a stable seat and presents it on every (re)initialize. The server re-binds the lease to that seat instead of minting one, and liveness for a proxied seat is the PROXY's pid, which is exactly "is this client still here". The proxy should distinguish "Session not found" (re-handshake, same seat, no server replacement) from "no server" (replace), which also removes the ~80 s stall. Raising keep-alive or disabling expiry would only move the cliff and leak sessions. It is a containment, not a fix.
⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether non-proxied HTTP clients (flo2's gateway, a browser) hit the same cliff. They talk to the server directly, so their own session handling decides, and they were not measured.
